headline: ACC Former Army Chief summoned by ACC over illegal wealth claims
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has summoned General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed to investigate allegations of acquiring illegal assets through corruption.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has summoned former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed for questioning regarding allegations of acquiring illegal wealth through corruption.
ACC Deputy Director Md. Aktarul Islam confirmed the summons on Sunday, stating that the investigation is ongoing to ensure a fair inquiry.
The former Army Chief has been directed to appear at the ACC head office on September 14, bringing a photocopy of his National Identity Card (NID).
A two-member investigation team has been formed, led by ACC Director Md. Abul Hasnat and member Deputy Director Mozammel Hossain.
The notice emphasizes that hearing the former Army Chief's statement is essential for a fair and thorough investigation into the irregularities and corruption allegations.
caption:
Former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed summoned by the ACC for questioning on illegal wealth allegations.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has summoned former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed for questioning regarding allegations of acquiring illegal wealth through corruption.

ACC Deputy Director Md. Aktarul Islam confirmed the summons on Sunday, stating that the investigation is ongoing to ensure a fair inquiry.

The former Army Chief has been directed to appear at the ACC head office on September 14, bringing a photocopy of his National Identity Card (NID).

A two-member investigation team has been formed, led by ACC Director Md. Abul Hasnat and member Deputy Director Mozammel Hossain.

The notice emphasizes that hearing the former Army Chief's statement is essential for a fair and thorough investigation into the irregularities and corruption allegations.

#Bangladesh #ACC #Corruption #ArmyChief #News

Source: Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Malaysia to [[hire 200,000 Bangladeshi workers]] in 6 months
headline: Malaysia to hire 200,000 Bangladeshi workers in 6 months
summary: State Minister Mir Shahe Alam announced the recruitment drive and a potential US$2 billion investment in renewable energy and halal food sectors.
details: State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam announced that Malaysia will recruit approximately 200,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next six months.
The recruitment process will be carried out through various agencies, with 10,000 of these workers being hired free of cost.
The manpower export process is expected to start in phases from the end of September and will be completed within the half-year timeframe.
Beyond labor, preparations are underway for Malaysia to invest about US$2 billion in Bangladesh's electric vehicles, solar panels, renewable energy, and halal food sectors.
The announcements followed a meeting between Malaysian High Commissioner Mohd Shuhada Othman and LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.
The two countries also discussed the registration of unregistered Bangladeshi workers currently in Malaysia, where about 8 lakh registered workers already reside.
Additionally, the meeting touched upon the potential visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Malaysia to further strengthen bilateral relations.
The State Minister also noted that approximately 10,000 Bangladeshi students are studying in Malaysia, while 1,000 Malaysian students are studying in medical colleges in Bangladesh.
caption:
200,000 jobs in Malaysia! 🇲🇾

State Minister Mir Shahe Alam reveals a massive recruitment drive for Bangladeshi workers.

State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam announced that Malaysia will recruit approximately 200,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next six months.

The recruitment process will be carried out through various agencies, with 10,000 of these workers being hired free of cost.

The manpower export process is expected to start in phases from the end of September and will be completed within the half-year timeframe.

Beyond labor, preparations are underway for Malaysia to invest about US$2 billion in Bangladesh's electric vehicles, solar panels, renewable energy, and halal food sectors.

The announcements followed a meeting between Malaysian High Commissioner Mohd Shuhada Othman and LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.

The two countries also discussed the registration of unregistered Bangladeshi workers currently in Malaysia, where about 8 lakh registered workers already reside.

Additionally, the meeting touched upon the potential visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Malaysia to further strengthen bilateral relations.

The State Minister also noted that approximately 10,000 Bangladeshi students are studying in Malaysia, while 1,000 Malaysian students are studying in medical colleges in Bangladesh.

#Bangladesh #Malaysia #Employment #JobOpportunities #Economy #BilateralRelations

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV
